items.title: Jensen Huang back at Nvidia, stock soars; Anthropic slides
items.summary: The 8:30 team is joined by Roundhill Investments Chief Investment Strategist Drew Pettit to discuss why washed-out sentiment doesn't mean a fundamental bottom, his $50-to-$250 bull-bear range on Anthropic, and how to handicap the "Jensen premium" coming back into Nvidia. Deirdre Bosa Live host Deirdre Bosa also joins to break down Silicon Valley's reaction to Huang's return and what it means for the AI trade.

items.title: Jensen Huang back as Nvidia CEO after 12 days: Shares surge 30%
items.summary:
Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi breaks down the stunning news of the morning: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstating founder Jensen Huang as CEO just 12 days after his resignation. Including his five takeaways on what the reversal says about corporate governance, the role Washington played in the decision, and the rally that's lifting the whole AI trade while sending AMD lower.

Brian is joined by New Street Research technology infrastructure analyst Antoine Chkaiban on the new checks around Huang and why he's still a buyer; "In the Loop" host Ejaz on key-man risk and whether the "Bank of Nvidia" reopens for neoclouds; EMJ Capital founder and president Eric Jackson, who calls the return a win for open-source AI; Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman on the board's credibility and Colette Kress's future; Moor Insights & Strategy founder and chief analyst Patrick Moorhead on the politics behind the ouster and why nothing changes for AMD for 18 months; and SlateStone Wealth partner and chief market strategist Kenny Polcari on whether this kicks off a year-end rally.

items.title: Alphabet Soars 6% as Jensen Huang’s Return to Nvidia Reignites AI Stocks
items.summary: Key TakeawaysAlphabet stock rose 6% as Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia sparked a rally in AI stocks, led by names like Taiwan Semiconductor and CoreWeave. Alphabet held up in Friday’s sell-off, so it had less ground to win back.

items.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO amid pressure from Trump, investors
items.summary: (Drops extraneous text in paragraph 2)  Nov 23 (Reuters) - Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO at the urging of US President Donald Trump in a stunning reversal following his resignation over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged spy for China, that roiled markets and the AI ecosystem. Huang's reinstatement sent the company's shares soaring 33%, with the board saying it unanimously approved his return and that it saw no national ‌security risk.

items.title: Nvidia Is Now Second To Apple In The World’s Most Valued Companies On Jensen Huang Optimism
items.summary: Nvidia’s market capitalization ticked to over $4 trillion on Monday following Jensen Huang’s reinstatement, making it the second most valuable company in the world.

items.title: The S&P 500 Just Fell Into a Correction. Your $3 Million Retirement Portfolio May Be Less Diversified Than You Think
items.summary: Owning 500 stocks feels safe until the market turns. A look inside one popular index fund shows how a handful of names can quietly steer your retirement, and why the same selloff hit two nearly identical funds very differently.
